mechanism_narrative: When the FEDFUNDS rate rises by more than 0.25% over the next month, investors anticipate higher future inflation, which lowers real equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > (current value + 0.25%) in the following month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the identified FEDFUNDS rise, or inflation surprises are not stronger than expected.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in PAYEMS (labor market activity) of at least 2% over two months predicts stronger consumer demand, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns in the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by ≥2% over the next two months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the PAYEMS expansion, or GDP growth is below expectations.

mechanism_narrative: When GDPC1 (real private demand) exceeds INDPRO (industrial production) by more than 5% in the prior quarter, it signals excess demand, leading to positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 > INDPRO + 5% in the previous quarter
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) when the GDPC1-INDPRO gap persists, or the gap reverses direction within the horizon.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) of at least 8% in a month indicates supply-side weakness, which typically precedes negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by ≥8% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) during the INDPRO decline, or production recovers faster than expected.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 4% for three consecutive months, it signals labor market strength and typically precedes a positive S&P 500 5-day forward return.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05) during the low UNRATE period, or other contrarian indicators are absent.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (labor) by at least 10% over the next quarter is interpreted as a dual recovery, predicting positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by ≥10% and PAYEMS increases by ≥10% over the next quarter
regime_hint: Dual recovery in housing and labor markets
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive (p > 0.05), or the interaction effect is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent CPIAUCSL (CPI) inflation above 3%, S&P 500 20-day forward returns tend to be negative due to expectations of rate hikes, unless offset by a strong FEDFUNDS response.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 3% for two consecutive months and FEDFUNDS remains below 4.5%
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when CPIAUCSL is high and FEDFUNDS is constrained.

mechanism_narrative: When RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 12% in a month, it indicates weak consumer demand and typically results in negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by ≥12% in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically negative (p > 0.05) during the RSAFS decline, or retail sales rebound rapidly.
